
══════════════════════════════════════════
  HUNT: Process Hollowing
══════════════════════════════════════════

  VERDICT     LIKELY HOLLOWING — MEM_PRIVATE at image base correlated with RWX protection
  Confidence  medium
  Score       1/2  (requires MEM_PRIVATE at the image base correlated with a second structural anomaly; single signals are leads only)
  Coverage    COMPLETE
  Review      high

  KEY SIGNALS

  [!] DETECTION  Correlated structural hollowing indicators
      2 independent structural signal(s) correlate at the same image base: MEM_PRIVATE at image
      base, RWX protection.

  [~] LEAD       MEM_PRIVATE memory at the image base
      The main module's image base is backed by MEM_PRIVATE memory, not a file-mapped MEM_IMAGE
      region.

  [~] LEAD       RWX protection at the image base
      The main module's image base carries RWX-family protection.

  WHY THIS VERDICT

  Inference
    2 independent structural signal(s) correlate at the same image base: MEM_PRIVATE at image base,
    RWX protection.

  Confidence: MEDIUM
    Any one of these signals alone has a plausible benign explanation (manual mapping, a
    capture-time read race, a JIT/packer using RWX). MEM_PRIVATE at the image base correlated with a
    missing/wiped MZ header AND/OR RWX protection at that same address is materially harder to
    explain away — the combination the module's own checks were designed to catch.

  Caveat
    Structural correlation is strong evidence but not a substitute for live-execution corroboration
    (no thread-context signal is available for this hunter).

  Use --verbose for the image base's VA/file offset, memory type/protection, header bytes, and module comparison.
